summary: Stabilize Connector SDK v1 by adding a signed, least-privilege, non-executing third-party plugin security boundary and strengthening provider import isolation without opening provider admission.

impacts.evidence: Permission grants are installation authority bound to an immutable artifact identity; tenant persistence is deliberately deferred, while existing connector accounts remain tenant scoped and no ambient host authority is introduced.
Descriptors and grants contain only bounded manifest, publisher, capability, secret-class, network and limit metadata; raw secret bytes, arbitrary remote bodies and PII payloads are absent.
Three additive Draft 2020-12 plugin security contracts are introduced. Existing Connector SDK v1 manifest/account/health/error contracts remain unchanged.
Task 025 adds no EventBus event type and changes no existing event envelope or payload contract.
Connector SDK major v1 is stabilized: root Connector, Runtime and SecretAccessor method surfaces are frozen by regression tests, while the isolated plugin boundary is separately versioned as v1.
Task 025 introduces no database migration and does not modify connector account, secret, catalog, order or event persistence.

Artifact SHA-256, Ed25519 publisher verification, exact permission grants, egress allowlists and resource ceilings are validated before an inert plan is produced; provider direct execution/network/filesystem escape imports are rejected by architecture checks.
Installation permission grants can only narrow the signed request and are bound to an exact version/digest. Sensitive operation approval remains owned by Task 017 and runtime enforcement by Task 029.
Stable publisher, key, artifact digest, connector version and grant metadata provide deterministic future audit identifiers without persisting raw credentials or provider response content.
No sync, reconciliation, inbox or idempotency algorithm changes. The security boundary only constrains how a future plugin may be admitted.
Third-party egress is declared as exact lower-case DNS host plus port and cannot use direct network imports. Actual DNS-resolution and egress enforcement remains Task 029.
Versioned memory, CPU time, wall time, output-size and concurrency ceilings define future sandbox observability/enforcement inputs without claiming runtime enforcement yet.

The change is code/contracts/docs only with no data migration. Rollback removes Task-025 verification support while provider admission remains disabled, so no executable third-party runtime state exists to migrate.

Tests cover digest/signature tamper, publisher trust, capability/secret/network escalation, exact network validation, frozen SDK root interfaces and architecture rejection of direct process/network/filesystem provider imports.
